title: Cargo Door Outer Skin Panel — Dent Blend-Out and Filler Repair
abstract: Blend-out and filler repair for ground handling dents in the outer skin panel of a cargo door, the most common damage on the type and normally closed at the line station.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the surface contour and the corrosion protection of the cargo door outer skin panel after a ground handling dent, without any structural reinforcement.
sections.damage_assessment: Measure the dent depth with the dial gauge and a straight edge, and measure its longest dimension across the surface. This repair is valid for a smooth dent up to 3 mm deep and up to 90 mm across, with no crease, no crack and no fastener inside the dent boundary. A dent with a crease line, a dent over a fastener row, or any dent on the door hinge line is outside the scope of this repair. Check the inside face of the panel for a matching deformation of the skin panel D5230111683975 and for a disbond of the strap D5230115372116 before the repair is accepted as cosmetic.
sections.repair_procedure: Clean the damaged area and an area of at least 200 mm around it. Blend out the dent edges to remove the stress concentration, keeping the blend depth inside the limit on the repair drawing and checking it with the depth gauge at each stage. Do not attempt to push the dent out from inside the door; the skin is bonded to the internal grid and a push repair will disbond it. Do an eddy current inspection of the blended area and of the boundary. Apply the surface protection of the standard practice to the blended surface. Fill the residual depression with the approved aerodynamic filler in layers not thicker than 0.5 mm, letting each layer cure before the next is applied. Sand the cured filler back to the surrounding contour and check the profile with the contour template on sheet 2. Where the splice plate D5230119841497 is inside the repair boundary, seal its edge again after sanding. Restore the paint scheme.
sections.inspection_requirements: No repeat inspection is required where the blended depth stays inside the limit and the eddy current inspection is clear. Where the blend reaches the limit, do a general visual inspection of the repair at every A-check for the first 2 000 flight cycles. A repair whose filler cracks or lifts must be stripped and re-done rather than filled over. Record the dent position and depth so that repeated damage at the same station can be raised with the ground handling agent.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Smooth dent up to 3 mm deep and up to 90 mm across, with no crease, no crack, no fastener inside the boundary and not on the hinge line.

type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit where the blend stays inside the drawing limit. A blend at the limit needs a general visual inspection at every A-check for 2 000 flight cycles.

Datum note: the rigged door position that the depth limits are measured against moves by up to 0.15 mm with the revised latch pin housing clearance of MOD-160915. That is inside the 0.25 mm tolerance of the dial gauge method and no limit in this repair changes because of it. The figure is recorded here so that the question is not reopened at the next revision of this repair.
